evidence.note: 'swapping can only happen at .await points, so code that spends a long time without reaching an .await will prevent other tasks from running.'
Clippy's lint list has await_holding_lock/refcell/invalid_type but no lint for blocking calls inside async fns.

rs-blocking-call-in-async.whyNotLinter: Clippy has no blocking-in-async lint. `disallowed_methods` could ban `std::thread::sleep` everywhere, including sync code where it is fine; whether code is inside an async context and whether a call blocks takes judgment.
rs-blocking-call-in-async.aiRelevance: High. Agents use `std::fs::read_to_string` and `std::thread::sleep` in async handlers because that is the std API they know best.
rs-blocking-call-in-async.expectedNoise: low — the blocking APIs are named, and sync functions are a listed negative.
rs-blocking-call-in-async.overlap: Duplicates rules/rust.performance.json rs-perf-blocking-in-async, which appeared in the working tree during this research (uncommitted). Keep only one; if the perf pack ships, drop this rule.

evidence.note: Lists the cancel-safe methods and the non-cancel-safe ones (read_exact, read_to_end, read_to_string, write_all; Mutex::lock, RwLock::read/write, Semaphore::acquire, Notify::notified).

rs-select-cancel-unsafe.whyNotLinter: Cancellation safety is a documented runtime property of each method, not part of its type. No clippy or rustc lint covers it.
rs-select-cancel-unsafe.aiRelevance: High. `loop { select! { r = stream.read_exact(&mut buf) => …, _ = shutdown.recv() => break } }` is a natural-looking pattern agents write for protocol loops. Data loss only shows under load.
rs-select-cancel-unsafe.expectedNoise: low — the method list is exact, and the pinned-outside-the-loop pattern is a listed negative.
rs-select-cancel-unsafe.evidenceStatus: single official B source for the exact API; needs a second B (or A from a repo) before shipping as built-in, or accept it on the strength of the vendor doc

evidence.note: 'A JoinHandle detaches the associated task when it is dropped' (source: tokio/src/runtime/task/join.rs). JoinHandle itself is not #[must_use], so rustc's unused_must_use doesn't fire.

rs-spawned-task-error-lost.whyNotLinter: Dropping a JoinHandle is legal and doesn't trigger a warning (not #[must_use]); clippy's `let_underscore_future` is about futures, not handles. Whether the task handles its own errors is a judgment about its body.
rs-spawned-task-error-lost.aiRelevance: Medium-high. Agents spawn background work with `tokio::spawn(async move { do_thing().await? ; Ok::<_, Error>(()) });` and never look at the result.
rs-spawned-task-error-lost.expectedNoise: low — the handle's fate and the body's error handling are both visible.
rs-spawned-task-error-lost.evidenceStatus: single official B source for the exact API; needs a second B (or A from a repo) before shipping as built-in, or accept it on the strength of the vendor doc

evidence.note: Overflow is 'an error'; debug builds panic, other builds may 'panic or silently wrap'.
Study of errors in code from 7 LLMs: numeric-overflow runtime errors are 43.9% of Rust runtime errors vs 4–6% in C/C++/Java.

rs-unsigned-subtraction-underflow.whyNotLinter: `clippy::arithmetic_side_effects` (restriction) flags every arithmetic operation. `implicit_saturating_sub` only rewrites an already-guarded subtraction. Whether the right side can exceed the left needs judgment about the values.
rs-unsigned-subtraction-underflow.aiRelevance: High. It is the dominant Rust runtime failure in LLM output in the one study found (C-grade), and agents write `len() - 1` reflexively.
rs-unsigned-subtraction-underflow.expectedNoise: med — many subtractions are safe for reasons outside the snippet; the question requires that nothing in the snippet rules underflow out, and it may need wording iteration.
rs-unsigned-subtraction-underflow.evidenceStatus: single official B source for the exact API; needs a second B (or A from a repo) before shipping as built-in, or accept it on the strength of the vendor doc

evidence.note: 'Calling this method with an out-of-bounds index is undefined behavior even if the resulting reference is not used' (library/core/src/slice/mod.rs).
Rustonomicon: unsafe code's soundness depends on invariants established by surrounding safe code (standard reference, not re-fetched).
Claims unsafe blocks are 3–5x more frequent in LLM Rust than in human code; unsourced. Lead only.

rs-unchecked-unsafe-on-unvalidated.whyNotLinter: Clippy checks for a SAFETY comment (`undocumented_unsafe_blocks`, restriction) and some transmute shapes, not whether the precondition actually holds. That takes reasoning about where values come from.
rs-unchecked-unsafe-on-unvalidated.aiRelevance: Medium-high. Agents reach for `get_unchecked`/`from_utf8_unchecked` when asked to optimize and justify them with confident but wrong SAFETY comments.
rs-unchecked-unsafe-on-unvalidated.expectedNoise: low — rare API family; correct uses usually show the bounds check or construction.

evidence.note: 'The Client holds a connection pool internally ... so it is advised that you create one and reuse it.'

rs-http-client-per-call.whyNotLinter: Constructing a client is legal; whether the function runs once or per request is a judgment about the call site. Clippy has no lint for it.
rs-http-client-per-call.aiRelevance: Medium-high. Agents write self-contained `async fn fetch_x(url) { let client = Client::new(); … }` helpers.
rs-http-client-per-call.expectedNoise: low — the constructor call and its location are visible.
rs-http-client-per-call.evidenceStatus: single official B source for the exact API; needs a second B (or A from a repo) before shipping as built-in, or accept it on the strength of the vendor doc
